summary: WAYLOAM can now check the public alpha channel from inside the app, show a structured changelog, and download a newer APK without exposing the private source repository.
highlights: Settings now has a dedicated Software Update area.
What’s New is grouped into Added, Changed, and Fixed sections.
Updates are fetched from the public wayloam-releases repository with no embedded GitHub token.
APK downloads use Android’s system Download Manager.
added: Settings screen with app version, update channel, release source, and update status.
Automatic update check when Settings opens, plus a manual Check again action.
Structured What’s New cards driven by public release metadata.
In-app APK download using Android Download Manager with download progress and Open Downloads handoff.
Public release manifest format for future alpha updates.
changed: Settings is accessible from Home without overcrowding the five-item ride navigation bar.
The release pipeline now targets the public 0xpix/wayloam-releases repository while keeping source code private.
Alpha releases are prepared for a dedicated stable signing key instead of runner-generated debug signing.
Version naming is simplified to v0.2.0.alpha without an extra alpha sequence suffix.
fixed: Corrected release URLs after the source repository rename from waylloam to wayloam.
Separated source-code distribution from APK distribution so the updater never needs credentials for the private repository.
